requirements.expected: The base class contains operand_A (int), operand_B (int), alu_op (Enum), and alu_result (int), plus the listed common methods.

requirements.expected: Display ALU information; exact content and formatting are not specified.

requirements.title: Implement logical ALU operations
requirements.text: Define logical_alu as a class derived from base_alu and support the listed logical operations.
requirements.expected: Support AND (0111), OR (1000), XOR (1001), shift left (1010), shift right (1011), rotate left (1100), and rotate right (1101). Exact shift/rotate semantics are not specified.
requirements.source: Operations and codes explicitly stated; execution details partly unspecified

requirements.title: Implement arithmetic ALU operations
requirements.text: Define arithmetic_alu as a class derived from base_alu and support the listed arithmetic operations.
requirements.expected: Support select data on port B (0000), increment data on port B (0001), decrement data on port B (0010), add without carry (0011), add with carry (0100), subtract without borrow (0101), and subtract with borrow (0110). Exact carry/borrow conventions are not specified.
requirements.source: Operations and codes explicitly stated; execution details partly unspecified

requirements.title: Define CPU class
requirements.text: Define a CPU class that contains logical and arithmetic ALU objects.
requirements.expected: The CPU class contains l_alu of type logical_alu and a_alu of type arithmetic_alu.

requirements.title: Reset CPU

requirements.source: Method explicitly named; effects require clarification

requirements.title: Calculate selected ALU operation

requirements.expected: Process the supplied operands and operation using the appropriate ALU object and return the result. Exact dispatch and error handling are not specified.
requirements.source: Method signature and return type explicitly stated; dispatch behavior inferred from system purpose

requirements.text: Represent ALU operation codes using an enum type.
requirements.expected: The operation field identifies the selected operation. The exact enum name and whether one shared enum is required are not specified.
requirements.source: Enum usage and codes stated; enum declaration details require clarification

requirements.expected: The package contains the CPU-related definitions.

operations.name: ADD without CARRY
operations.result: result = A + B; carry = unsigned carry out

operations.name: ADD with CARRY
operations.result: result = A + B + carry; carry = unsigned carry out

operations.name: SUB without BORROW
operations.result: result = A - B; carry = borrow out

operations.name: SUB with BORROW
operations.result: result = A - B - carry; carry = borrow out

operations.name: Rotate left
operations.result: result = A rotated left by B[4:0] within 32 bits

operations.name: Rotate right
operations.result: result = A rotated right by B[4:0] within 32 bits

constraints.text: Each class must be placed in a separate file.
A cpu_pkg package must contain all CPU-related definitions.
A simple program must import cpu_pkg and test the CPU and its objects.
The common base_alu properties are operand_A (int), operand_B (int), alu_op (Enum), and alu_result (int).
logical_alu and arithmetic_alu are derived from base_alu.
CPU contains logical_alu l_alu and arithmetic_alu a_alu.
Operation codes are presented as 4-bit values from 4'b0000 through 4'b1101 for the listed operations.
Use of extern for class functions is optional.
The assignment does not specify detailed behavior for invalid or unsupported operation codes.
The assignment does not define exact reset/initialization values or sequence.
Carry and borrow inputs/outputs and their conventions are not fully defined.
Shift/rotate operand mapping, amount source, and data width are not specified.
The assignment does not specify operand width, signedness, overflow, or underflow behavior beyond the declared int types.
The enum name and exact declaration are not specified, although operation properties/parameters use an Enum type.
Exact method signatures and return behavior for display, load_operand_A, load_operand_B, and initialize are not fully specified.
The exact behavior of selecting data on port B is not elaborated beyond the operation name and code.
For implementation planning, keep all unspecified behavior explicitly marked and request clarification before treating a proposed behavior as a requirement.
Use stable requirement/interface/operation IDs across revisions when the item remains semantically the same.

open_questions.question: What is the exact SystemVerilog enum type name and where should it be declared?
open_questions.answer: D-001: Declare typedef enum logic [3:0] {...} alu_op_t; once in cpu_pkg, with the 14 listed codes (OP_SEL_B=4'b0000 ... OP_ROR=4'b1101). Both alu_op and Calc's operation use alu_op_t.

open_questions.question: For each operation, which input operand(s) are used and in what order?
open_questions.answer: D-002: in1/operand_A is the first operand, in2/operand_B the second. Binary ops compute A op B; SUB is A - B. Port-B ops (SEL_B, INC_B, DEC_B) use operand_B only.

open_questions.question: For shift and rotate operations, where does the shift/rotation amount come from?
open_questions.answer: D-003: Shifts and rotates act on operand_A; the amount is operand_B[4:0] (0 to 31). Amount 0 returns A unchanged.

open_questions.question: What operand width and signedness should apply to shifts, rotations, and arithmetic results?
open_questions.answer: D-004: Resolved by the language: the spec declares int, which is 32-bit, signed, 2-state in SystemVerilog. Arithmetic wraps modulo 2^32. Shift right is logical (>>), rotates work on 32 bits.

open_questions.question: How is carry-in supplied for ADD with CARRY, and how should carry-out be represented?
open_questions.answer: D-005: Add a bit carry property to arithmetic_alu (status flag, like a CPU carry flag). ADDC computes A + B + carry. ADD, ADDC, SUB, SUBB all update carry with the unsigned carry/borrow out. Calc's signature stays as in the spec.

open_questions.question: How is borrow-in supplied for SUB with BORROW, and how should borrow-out be represented?
open_questions.answer: D-006: The same carry bit acts as borrow. SUBB computes A - B - carry. Borrow out = 1 when the unsigned subtraction needs a borrow.

open_questions.question: What should initialize() set, and what should the default values of the ALU properties be?
open_questions.answer: D-007: initialize() sets operand_A = 0, operand_B = 0, alu_op = OP_SEL_B, alu_result = 0 (and carry = 0 in arithmetic_alu). new() calls initialize().

open_questions.question: What exact state should CPU Reset clear or initialize?
open_questions.answer: D-008: CPU.Reset() calls initialize() on l_alu and a_alu. It does not re-create the objects.

open_questions.question: What should happen when an unsupported or unassigned opcode is supplied?
open_questions.answer: D-009: Codes 4'b1110 and 4'b1111 are invalid. Calc returns 0, sets alu_result = 0 in neither ALU, and prints an $error naming the code. No state changes.

open_questions.question: What exact output and formatting should display() produce?
open_questions.answer: D-010: display() prints one line: [<class>] op=<op.name()> A=<%0d> B=<%0d> result=<%0d> (arithmetic_alu adds  carry=<0/1>).

open_questions.question: What are the exact parameter and return types of load_operand_A(), load_operand_B(), and initialize()?
open_questions.answer: D-011: function void load_operand_A(int value), function void load_operand_B(int value), function void initialize(), function void display().

open_questions.question: What exact signature and dispatch behavior should CPU.Calc use for operation and Result?
open_questions.answer: D-012: function int Calc(int in1, int in2, alu_op_t operation). Codes 0000-0110 go to a_alu, 0111-1101 to l_alu. Calc loads operands and op into that ALU, calls its execute(), returns its alu_result.

open_questions.question: Should the ALU class functions be declared extern, and if so, which functions?
open_questions.answer: D-013: extern is not used (it is optional). Methods are defined inside each class.

open_questions.question: What exact set of definitions must cpu_pkg contain?
open_questions.answer: D-014: cpu_pkg defines alu_op_t and includes base_alu.svh, logical_alu.svh, arithmetic_alu.svh, cpu.svh in that order. Each class stays in its own file.

open_questions.question: What minimum test cases or acceptance criteria are required for submission?
open_questions.answer: D-015: Self-checking test program: every opcode at least once, plus the boundary vectors in alu_spec.json (wrap-around, carry chain, shift by 0/31/32, rotate wrap), Reset, and an invalid opcode. Prints PASS/FAIL counts; exit criterion = 0 failures.

open_questions.question: Should arithmetic operations expose overflow, carry, or borrow flags in addition to alu_result?
open_questions.answer: D-016: Expose only the carry flag (D-005), read with function bit get_carry(). No overflow flag.

open_questions.question: For operation 4'b0000, where should selected port-B data be stored or returned?
open_questions.answer: D-017: SEL_B writes operand_B into alu_result.

open_questions.question: What should happen if CPU or an ALU method is called before its objects/state are initialized?
open_questions.answer: D-018: CPU.new() constructs l_alu and a_alu; base_alu.new() calls initialize(), so no object is ever used uninitialised.

methods.does: computes alu_result from alu_op; overridden by derived classes
methods.note: added design element (not in assignment) so CPU can dispatch polymorphically

methods.sig: function int Calc(int in1, int in2, alu_op_t operation)
methods.does: 0000-0110 -> a_alu, 0111-1101 -> l_alu: load A, B, op; execute(); return alu_result. Invalid code: $error, return 0, no state change.
